speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when your gait and limb ataxia first started, and have you noticed any other neurological symptoms like vision changes or tremors?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any difficulty swallowing, slurred speech, or changes in your vision? Also, do you have a history of alcohol use or any recent head injuries?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, are you experiencing any new headaches, fever, or severe muscle weakness? I need to rule out a serious infection like PML, so I will also request a brain MRI. REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature is Normothermic; Blood Pressure, Heart Rate, and Respiratory Rate are all within normal range. Neurological Examination: Ataxic gait noted; Right Upper Limb Strength is 4/5; Coordination tests show evidence of ataxia. Brain MRI: Findings show lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). Comments: T1/T2 images show multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings confirm lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML), a serious opportunistic infection linked to your natalizumab use. Do you have any immediate questions about stopping your medication, or would you like me to explain the next steps in managing this condition? DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML)
